In iOS 27, Apple says it has put special care into making its software "more responsive, more reliable, and more delightful." This release includes a number of fixes that should make your iPhone run more smoothly, including an update targeting network switching.

iOS 27 makes switching between Wi-Fi and cellular smoother than ever

Apple says that under the broad theme of "platform improvements," the company has done extensive work in iOS 27 to make your iPhone run faster.

The speed boost is evident in several areas, and one that Apple specifically highlights is network switching.

In the past, whenever your iPhone switched between a Wi-Fi network and cellular, there was always an annoying delay.

When you step out of your home and leave Wi-Fi range, your iPhone still thinks it's connected to Wi-Fi, so it fails to switch to cellular in time.

The result is that you have no data connection at all for a brief period.

When this happens, the common fix is to open Control Center and temporarily turn off Wi-Fi, forcing your iPhone to switch to cellular immediately.

However, in iOS 27, you shouldn't need to do this anymore.

Apple says: "During network switching, transitions between cellular and Wi-Fi are smoother than ever."

Basically, iOS 27 makes your iPhone smarter, knowing when to switch from Wi-Fi to cellular, and vice versa. After two months of beta testing, it looks like Apple has indeed delivered on this promise.

So far, I can hardly recall needing to manually turn off Wi-Fi in iOS 27. Even during network transitions, my iPhone maintains a stable connection. Hopefully, once iOS 27 rolls out officially, all users will enjoy the same experience.

How has your network switching experience been in iOS 27 beta? Let us know in the comments.
